title: An interval-wise partite matching family is bounded by the product of the pattern parameters
author: Lisa Sauermann; Dmitrii Zakharov
work: A Sharp Ramsey Theorem for Ordered Hypergraph Matchings
difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 359-362: for a positive integer r, an ordered partition lambda of r and parameters attached to the patterns, any interval-wise lambda-partite family of edges has size at most the product of those parameters. The proof (source lines 365-377) is a covering argument whose three steps the statement does not show: the edges are encoded by the tuple of their smallest vertices in each block of the cutting of the order, so that pairwise disjointness makes those tuples distinct; the resulting point set is then split into the finitely many quadrants indexed by the sign patterns compatible with the ordered partition, and each quadrant is bounded by its own parameter, which is where the monotonicity of the parameters is used; finally the multidimensional Erdos-Szekeres theorem is invoked to see that every point lies in one of those quadrants. The statement records only the product bound.
